quick_english: Now the eleventh chapter: Arjuna asks to make directly seen the very meaning stated in the preceding chapter, since what is understood through teaching becomes clear when mounted by direct cognition; therefore these statements and replies are spoken. Arjuna said: for my grace you spoke the supreme secret called self-knowledge; by that speech this delusion of mine is gone.

What again, by clearer manifestation and speech?

quick_english: Slay Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and other world-heroes; they have been slain by me, so do not be distressed; fight, and you will conquer rivals in battle. You fed the secret summarized in this chapter; may it be for those capable of immediate awareness. How much labor of line-writing; may we rest in stability. Here what was said by me: when they are slain, you, glorious one, be instrument. Thus by the Lord that was replied to what was said earlier by Arjuna: we do not know this; which of us is greater, and so on.

quick_english: The sages remember your divine and wondrous former deeds; no other is doer of the world; you alone are sustainer, ordainer, and all-pervading Bhava.

cite_parts: śrībhagavānuvāca   mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt
tejomayaṃ viśvamanantamādyaṃ yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam

quick_english: Not by Veda, sacrifice, study, nor by gifts, nor by rites, nor by severe austerities can such a form be seen by me in the human world by other than you, O Kuru hero.
cite_parts: na vedayajñādhigamanairna dānai- rna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ
evaṃrūpaṃ śakyamāhaṃ nṛloke draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra

quick_english: Let there be no distress for you, nor confusion, having seen this terrible fierce form of mine; with fear gone and pleased mind, again you behold that very gentle form of mine.
cite_parts: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhata bhūd dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoramugraṃ  mamedam
vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvaṃ tadeva me rūpamidaṃ  prapaśya

quick_english: Sanjaya said that Vasudeva, having spoken thus to Arjuna, showed his own form again, consoled the frightened one, and became the great soul of gentle form.
cite_parts: saṃjaya uvāca   ityarjunaṃ vāsudevastathoktvā svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ
āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenaṃ bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā

quick_english: Arjuna said that having seen this gentle human form of Krishna, he is now restored, of sound mind, and returned to his nature; at the end of total withdrawal the Lord gives the supremely peaceful form, the state of Brahman-principle, and thus in conclusion the Lord's gentleness.
cite_parts: arjuna uvāca   dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tavasaumyaṃ janārdana
idānīmasmi  saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ
sakalopasaṃhārānte paramapraśāntarūpāṃ brahmatattvasthitiṃ  dadāti-ityupasaṃhāre bhagavataḥ saumyatā

quick_english: The blessed Lord said: this form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods always desire to see this form.
cite_parts: śrībhagavānuvāca   sudurdarśamidaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama
devā apyasya  rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

quick_english: I am not to be seen in such a form by the Vedas, nor by austerity, nor by gift, nor by sacrifice; you have seen me as I am.
cite_parts: nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā
śakya evaṃvidho  draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavānasi māṃ yathā

quick_english: By undivided devotion I can be known, seen, and entered in truth in such a form, O Arjuna, scorcher of foes.
cite_parts: bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya hyahamevaṃvidho'rjuna
jñātuṃ  draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa

quick_english: He who does my works, is devoted to me, is free from attachment, and is without enmity toward all beings reaches me, O Pandava. For those whose devotion shines forth toward no other knowable pleasant thing, Vasudeva approaches them; all. From the wonder of the previously stated teaching, the world-souled Vasudeva-principle descends effortlessly into the path of knowing. Auspicious. 60.
cite_parts: matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ
nirvairaḥ  sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava
avidyamānānyajñeyaramaṇīyā yeṣāṃ bhaktiḥ parisphurati teṣāṃ  māṃ prapadyate vāsudevaḥ sarvam  ityādipūrvābhihitopadeśacamatkārāt viśvātmakaṃ  vāsudevatattvamayatnata eva bodhapadavīmavataratīti śivam

label: 11-sangraha
quick_english: Here is the summary verse: through recognition of the unity of consciousness arising from pure, impure, and mixed states, the sage who sees earth, midworld, and the three worlds with equality is equal.
cite_parts: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   śuddhāśuddhavimiśrotthasaṃvidaikyavimarśanāt
bhūrbhuvaḥ  svastrayaṃ paśyansamatvena samo muniḥ
iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe ekādaśo'dhyāyaḥ
